item: The ML-DSA custody key is made once, 0600 from its first byte, and a pair written in the clear is wrapped in place
summary: The two R449 stated limits on the ML-DSA key file are closed. HybridSigner._load_or_create_mldsa now creates the pair through src.custody.keyfile.create_new (a private copy at 0600 linked into place, so two first callers end with ONE pair, never the last writer's) instead of write_bytes then chmod, and a pair written in the clear before the passphrase existed is wrapped in place on its first load under one through keyfile.replace_in_place: the same pair, read back and compared (public and secret halves, and the form) before it replaces anything. key_protection reports what the file holds now. A wrap that cannot land (a link, a read-only folder) is refused before the copy is sealed and its stand-down reads the unchanged file without a second scrypt, so a stuck wrap costs no extra derivation on each load. Stated limit kept in docs/SECURITY.md: an ML-DSA file is wrapped only when a signer loads it. Thirteen mutants each turn a named test red. Release-notes line: on an install with a passphrase the post-quantum custody key is now made once and encrypted in place like the Ed25519 key.
